channel.title: The Grant Desk - Fellowships, Journalism & Writers, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Fellowships, Journalism & Writers, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: IAS CEU: Global Invisible University Artist and Writer in Residence Fellowships 2027/28 (Budapest, EUR 2,000 a month) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Institute for Advanced Study, Central European University (IAS CEU)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: Net allowance of EUR 2,000 a month, plus accommodation at the Raoul Wallenberg Guesthouse and/or office space at IAS CEU as available. Travel and health insurance are not covered.

Two residential fellowships within the Global Invisible University programme: one Writer in Residence (poetry, prose, drama, screen and playwriting) and one Visual or New Media Artist in Residence (from painting and film to digital art, computer graphics and interactive art).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence 2027-28 (NYPL, Harlem; USD 35,000 long-term or USD 3,000 a month short-term; playwrights and creative writers eligible) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, The New York Public Library
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Long-term fellowship: USD 35,000 stipend. Short-term fellowship: USD 3,000 per month for one to three months. No application fee mentioned.

Residential fellowships for work on the history, politics, literature and culture of peoples of African descent that needs the Schomburg Center's collections.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027, "Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet" (funded six-week residency for researchers, creatives and practitioners) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Monthly allowance for the six-week residency (figure not published: researchers get standard Humboldt fellowship rates, creatives and practitioners a competitive honorarium), travel allowance to and from Germany, accommodation at Schloss Wiepersdorf and a Berlin aparthotel, and a budget for public formats. No family allowance. No application fee.

Each year the Humboldt Foundation brings twelve people from research, the arts and civil society together to work on one topic and find new ways of communicating it to audiences beyond academia. The 2027 topic is Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Los Angeles Reporting Collective: LARC 2027 Fellowship (Southern California, USD 600 stipend) (closes 23 Nov)
item.description:
Los Angeles Reporting Collective (LARC)
Deadline: 23 Nov 2026
Award: USD 600 project stipend, paid on completing the training phase, with possible extra funding for project expenses

Yearlong journalism training and mentorship programme for local reporters and nonfiction storytellers. Fellows get 12 free workshops (8 online, 4 in person in Los Angeles), a one-on-one mentor, newsroom shadowing and free conference access, then produce their own project with a USD 600 stipend.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MPI Short Film Lab 2027: narrative short film lab with fellowship grants and a USD 10,000 script grant (theme: For the Greater Good?) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
Moving Picture Institute (MPI)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026, 23:59 PST
Award: Filmmakers accepted into the lab receive fellowship grants (amount not published). One official selection receives a USD 10,000 grant, which includes MPI acquiring the script for further development. Travel support for the Los Angeles summit is not mentioned. No application fee mentioned.

The Moving Picture Institute is a production company and talent incubator that makes films about human freedom. Its Short Film Lab takes writer-directors from a concept to a finished short script, and can lead to production as an MPI Original film. THEME 2027: For the Greater Good?

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Gordon N. Fisher / JHR Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (Massey College, Toronto; for a journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Massey College, University of Toronto, with Journalists for Human Rights (JHR)
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: CAD 4,900 per month for the eight-month university year, all University of Toronto fees, and round-trip economy airfare to and from Toronto. No application fee mentioned.

One place alongside the William Southam Journalism Fellows at Massey College, University of Toronto, reserved for a journalist from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East. The fellow spends the academic year in Toronto auditing university courses and taking part in college life.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: LCC-CBA Journalism Fellowship 2027 (CAD 40,000 for four long-form articles on law and justice in Canada) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
Law Commission of Canada and Canadian Bar Association
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026
Award: CAD 40,000 stipend, paid quarterly on submission of each completed article. No application fee mentioned.

A one-year fellowship for a journalist to report in depth on how the law affects people's lives in Canada, now in its third year. WHO: journalists based in Canada with at least five years of full-time work experience who want to deepen their knowledge of the justice system.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: William Southam Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (Massey College, University of Toronto; CAD 4,900 a month for eight months) (closes 1 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Massey College, University of Toronto
Deadline: 1 Feb 2027
Award: CAD 4,900 per month for the eight-month university year (CAD 39,200), all university fees, and book expenses of up to CAD 600. No application fee mentioned.

Up to three mid-career journalists spend an academic year at Massey College, a graduate college within the University of Toronto, auditing courses of their choice and taking part in college life.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Schloss Wiepersdorf Individual and Collaborative Fellowships 2028 (Brandenburg; EUR 1,200/month plus room and board) (closes 15 Apr 2027)
item.description:
Schloss Wiepersdorf (state of Brandenburg)
Deadline: 15 Apr 2027, 23:59 CEST
Award: EUR 1,200 per month stipend, a one-time EUR 480 material grant, room and board, and German visa costs where needed. No application fee.

Three-month residential fellowships at Schloss Wiepersdorf for artists, writers, composers and scholars from Germany and abroad. Fellows get room, board, a EUR 1,200 monthly stipend and a material grant; fine artists get a studio where space allows.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Yale Law School Information Society Project: Resident Fellowship 2027-2028 (closes 10 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Yale Law School, Information Society Project (ISP)
Deadline: 10 Jan 2027
Award: USD 70,000 per year plus Yale benefits and a travel stipend. No application fee.

Postdoctoral resident fellowships at Yale ISP for scholars of law and technology, with AI as a stated priority alongside the digital public sphere, content moderation, privacy, antitrust and algorithmic governance.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Folger Institute Artistic Research Fellowships 2027-28 (USD 4,000 to 5,000 per month) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Folger Shakespeare Library (Folger Institute)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 4,000 per virtual month or USD 5,000 per onsite month.

Artistic research fellowships for artists whose work needs primary research on the early modern world (about 1400 to 1800) and its legacies, using the Folger's collections. ELIGIBILITY: any artist; no degree required and no citizenship rule stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (Columbia Journalism School) (closes 4 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Spencer Fellowship at Columbia Journalism School
Deadline: 4 Feb 2027
Award: Residential stipend USD 85,000 or non-residential stipend USD 43,000, plus a USD 7,500 travel and research budget. Non-residential fellows also get airfare and hotel for required NYC trips. No application fee.

The Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship, based at Columbia Journalism School, supports ambitious, research-savvy storytellers producing books, magazine features, documentaries and podcasts that deepen public understanding of critical issues in education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (University of Michigan) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 85,000 stipend plus USD 5,000 relocation (figures from secondary listings; confirm on the official site).

An academic-year fellowship for mid-career journalists to pursue a study project at the University of Michigan, with seminars and programming at Wallace House. DEADLINES: international applicants 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm ET; US applicants 1 February 2027. No application fee stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) (closes 9 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
Deadline: 9 Jan 2027
Award: USD 87,500 stipend over 9.5 months, plus USD 5,000 for travel and housing, health insurance and a childcare subsidy. No application fee.

An academic-year fellowship at MIT for journalists covering science, health, technology or the environment, with seminars, MIT and Harvard courses and a self-directed study project.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Open Notebook Early-Career Fellowship 2027 (remote)
item.description: The Open Notebook · deadline 31 Oct 2026 · USD 6,600 stipend over the twelve-month part-time fellowship, plus one-on-one mentoring from an experienced science journalist and published clips at The Open Notebook. No application fee.
